findings.claim: The Q1 WHY-NOT-B rationale states a factual absolute about the passage that the passage itself contradicts: it says the text 'never mentions habitat, species or wetland value', but paragraph 1 explicitly concedes that a rival, non-hydrological argument for beavers exists and names its subject.
findings.evidence: Q1 rationale, WHY-NOT-B: 'habitat and wetland value is the most familiar real-world case for beaver reintroduction, so a passage-blind reader will consider it, but this text argues entirely inside flood hydrology and never mentions habitat, species or wetland value.' Passage, paragraph 1: 'The arithmetic is easy to carry in the head, and it has done more for the case than any argument about willow ever did.' Willow is a species, and 'any argument about willow' is precisely the vegetation/ecology case for beavers that the storage arithmetic is said to have outcompeted. Sorrel also names vegetation management directly: 'Where the dams end up can be nudged, she says, by fencing, by planting and by leaving some tributaries to themselves'.
findings.why: Does not flip the pedagogy verdict. Option B ('restores a wetland whose real value the arithmetic of flood storage was never going to capture') is marginally more live than the rationale admits — the willow clause concedes such arguments were made — but the passage never endorses the wetland-value thesis and argues its own case entirely in flood hydrology, so key C remains the single best main-idea answer by a wide margin. The defect is an over-absolute word ('never mentions ... species') in the teaching payload, not a key error; MINOR_FIXES already signals residual rationale work.

findings.claim: The rarity framing and the event count will not reconcile: the passage sets up the rare-storm analysis with a once-in-a-working-life standard, then instantiates it as fourteen events inside a nine-year record whose ordinary-storm rate the passage itself puts at six or seven a winter.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 3: 'Then Sorrel's group stopped counting ordinary storms and looked at the rare ones. A defence at the bottom of a valley is not built for the rain that comes six times a season but for the storm that comes once in a working life, and it was in those that stored volume stopped predicting anything. Across the fourteen largest events in the record, the drop in peak height at Millstake bore almost no relation to how much water the dams upstream could hold.' The record is nine years ('Over nine years the hydrologist Anneke Sorrel and her group followed eleven headwater sub-catchments'), and ordinary storms run at 'six or seven times a winter' (~54-63 over the record). Fourteen events in nine years is ~1.5 per year — roughly the top quarter of the storm population, not the once-in-a-working-life event the preceding sentence makes the design standard.
findings.why: Does not flip the integrated verdict. The anaphor 'those' can be read charitably as 'the rare ones' operationalised as the record's largest fourteen, which is what a real nine-year study could actually do, and no option or key depends on the rarity rate — Q1 key C says only 'in the rarest storms', which is true relative to this record. It is a reconciliation wrinkle of exactly the class MINOR_NOTES exists to carry, not a contradiction that makes a distractor defensible.

findings.claim: Paragraph 2 attributes a single-outlet gauge reading to each of eleven sub-catchments without flagging the referent switch, so the study's measurement geometry does not resolve on a literal read.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 2: 'the peak that reached the gauge at Millstake was lower than before the beavers, and it arrived later. That held in all eleven sub-catchments, the steep peaty ones and the gentle grazed ones alike.' Millstake is a single point downstream of every tributary, per paragraph 3: 'water entering the highest of them takes the better part of a day longer to reach Millstake than water entering the lowest'. One gauge at one outlet cannot yield eleven per-sub-catchment results; the per-sub-catchment claim must rest on the separately mentioned 'gauging method common to all of them', which the sentence never re-introduces.
findings.why: Does not flip the integrated verdict and does not touch a key. Q2's key A mirrors the passage's own wording ('The peak reaching the gauge was lower and later than before the beavers, in all eleven sub-catchments alike') and inherits the same compression, so no distractor becomes defensible and A stays the single best answer. A compressed-referent readability wrinkle, already within the scope of MINOR_NOTES.

findings.claim: The Q4 WHY-NOT-D rationale rests on a false dichotomy and so undersells why D is wrong; D's mechanism is close to the passage's own account of blunting rather than foreign to it.
findings.evidence: Q4 option D: 'Water from the higher tributaries arrives too late to be counted in the peak that the gauge records.' Q4 rationale, WHY-NOT-D: 'The text says nothing of the sort; late arrival is what spreads the flood out, not what hides it from the gauge.' But the passage's stated premise is exactly differential lateness — 'water entering the highest of them takes the better part of a day longer to reach Millstake than water entering the lowest' — and a contribution arriving a day after the others is by definition outside the recorded peak. Spreading the flood out and contributions falling outside the peak are the same mechanism described at two scales, not alternatives. The upstream blind gate reached the same reading: G-STEM on q:4 records 'D is a genuine competing consequence of the same premise'.
findings.why: Does not flip the pedagogy verdict and does not threaten key sanity. D's actual fault is that it drops the dam-distribution element the stem is fishing for and adds an unsupported claim about what the gauge counts, while B ('Water from different tributaries takes different amounts of time to arrive, so spread-out dams keep the peaks from coinciding') is the join the text sets up and withholds. The rationale reaches the right verdict by a weaker argument than the item deserves — a teaching-payload quality note, consistent with MINOR_FIXES.
